subject: TRANSCRIPT EXTRACTION: let a user actually get their record out, and prove deletion
description:
Scoped 2026-08-08 in ~/hexworth-shared/User-History/. Depends on #300 (there is nothing to extract until the transcript has a canonical shape). TRIGGERED BY A MEASURED DEFECT IN TRIAL RUN: candidateId and sessionId are plain JS variables (web/index.html:310-311, never persisted), POST /candidate always INSERTs with no lookup by email (api/main.py:152-157), and there is no GET /candidate/{id}/sessions. Net effect: refresh the tab and the record is unreachable -- not exportable AND not deletable, since DELETE /candidate/{id} needs the same lost id, while llm_call still holds the full resume text until the retention purge. The same question is unanswered platform-wide: a Hexworth student has no way to obtain their own record. Scope covers format (machine-readable + human-readable), authentication of the request, what is INCLUDED vs excluded (Dr Hex chat excluded by prior decision, research data excluded by consent), and deletion receipts. See User-History/02-transcript-extraction-scope.md
[2026-08-08 21:36] SCOPE CLARIFIED 2026-08-08: since #300 is a COLLEGE transcript, extraction is not only a privacy obligation, it is the PRIMARY INTENDED USE -- a student hands this to an employer or another institution. Raises the bar on format stability and on being able to state what a given document asserted when it was issued. The Trial Run identity defect that exposed this is unchanged and still fixable independently (email lookup + GET /candidate/{id}/sessions + persist the id).
